testcase: JS build one package with workspace dependencies
query:
title: Build just my JavaScript package

question: I'm working on @azure/contoso-search in azure-sdk-for-js. How can I install dependencies and build that package together with its local dependencies instead of building the whole repository?
ground_truth: Run pnpm install at the repository root, then pnpm turbo build --filter=@azure/contoso-search... --token 1. The trailing ... includes the package's local dependencies. Use the full npm package name in the filter; a repository-wide build is unnecessary for this scoped change.

testcase: JS select Node and browser test targets
query:
title: Run the right JavaScript test target

question: I'm in a JavaScript SDK package directory. How do I run its Node tests, its browser tests, or both?
ground_truth: Run pnpm test for both Node and browser tests. Use pnpm test:node or pnpm test:browser to target one environment. Recorded tests use playback by default unless TEST_MODE selects another mode; selecting the browser target does not itself enable live testing.

testcase: JS distinguish playback live and record modes
query:
title: Choose the right mode for recorded SDK tests

question: For JS SDK tests that use the recorder, which TEST_MODE should I use to reuse existing responses offline, call the real service without saving recordings, or refresh recordings? Do the last two modes provision resources for me?
ground_truth: Use TEST_MODE=playback to replay existing recordings without requests to the real service, TEST_MODE=live to call the real service without saving recordings, and TEST_MODE=record to call it and save recordings. Recorded tests normally default to playback. Live and record modes both require provisioned test resources and the package's documented resource/authentication environment variables; selecting a mode does not create resources or grant access. Run the package's applicable test command after setting the mode.

testcase: JS distinguish migration acceptance from patch compatibility
query:
title: Interpret the migration guide's accepted breaking changes

question: Consider a hypothetical ARM JavaScript SDK migration from Swagger to TypeSpec with upgraded common types and removal of an unreferenced model. The migration guide calls these acceptable. Does that permit a patch release and blanket suppression of all breaking-change findings?
ground_truth: No. The guide's accepted-change section is specific to Swagger-to-TypeSpec migration and states that these changes are shipped in a new major version. Common-types upgrades and removal of unreferenced models are listed in that context, not as blanket permission for a patch release or to suppress unrelated findings. Classify each API difference against the guide, preserve compatibility where the guide provides a customization, and assess the complete diff and appropriate version with the SDK reviewers. The guide is not evidence that a particular release has been approved.

expected_references.title: JS TypeSpec migration: breaking changes that can be accepted

testcase: JS publish recordings and update their asset pointer
query:
title: Make new recordings available to CI

question: In a JS package using recorder 4.x with an existing assets.json, what should I do after recording new test responses so CI retrieves those recordings rather than the previous asset tag?
ground_truth: From the package directory, run npx dev-tool test-proxy push after recording and reviewing the new recordings. The command pushes recordings to the assets repository and updates the package's assets.json tag. Include that assets.json update in the SDK change so CI retrieves the new recordings. Local recording files alone do not move CI to the new asset tag; verify that you have the documented assets-repository permissions.

expected_references.title: JS testing: existing package recording push

testcase: JS third-party runtime dependency needs approval
query:
title: Add a new runtime dependency to a shipped JS SDK

question: My package has sdk-type client and needs a new third-party runtime dependency that isn't in the repository allow-list. Can I just add it to dependencies if the package builds?
ground_truth: No. A new third-party runtime dependency in an in-scope shipped client or management library needs approval. After approval, update eng/approved-third-party-dependencies.yml under allowed for repository-wide use or exceptions for named packages, then add the dependency using the repository's pnpm workflow. The ts-package-json-approved-dependencies ESLint rule checks dependencies during pnpm lint and CI. Building alone does not satisfy this requirement.

expected_references.title: Post-generation steps: adding a new third-party runtime dependency

testcase: JS generated code is not a release-ready package
query:
title: Prepare a generated JavaScript SDK for review

question: The TypeScript emitter generated my new package successfully. Is that sufficient to send the package for release, or what repository work is still needed?
ground_truth: Generation is only the starting point. Build the package, replace the empty sample test with meaningful service tests and manage their recordings, improve the README, prepare samples, update the changelog and semantic version, and configure the package's CI artifact entry. Run formatting, lint, build, and applicable tests and submit the resulting changes for team review. Successful code generation alone is not release approval or evidence of publication.

expected_references.title: What to do after generating the SDK code
